_comment: PMFreak consumer lock for the frozen AOC packaged artifacts (P0-PKG-04). Records repository, commit, version and SHA-256 of every installed artifact, as required by the pmfreak.obligations block of the frozen aoc.cross-repository-integration@1.0.0 contract shipped inside the @aoc/protocol tarball. Verified by scripts/check-packaged-aoc-artifacts.mjs. P0-PKG-05 additionally removed the retained local copies; ownership of what they contained is recorded in governance-ownership.lock.json. This file records identity; it authorizes no publication or release.

localSourceFallback.rationale: The canonical @aoc/protocol and @aoc-enterprise/runtime are the frozen packaged artifacts recorded below. Falling back to a repository-local source copy — under any specifier, alias or resolution path — would silently restore the pre-P0-PKG-04 state in which no import crossed a real package boundary, while the evidence in this file continued to assert that it did. There is no permitted fallback, not even a temporary or diagnostic one.
localSourceFallback.enforcedBy: npm run check:packaged-aoc-artifacts (scripts/check-packaged-aoc-artifacts.mjs), with negative controls in tests/packaged-aoc-artifact-gate.test.mjs

localCopies.rationale: P0-PKG-04 retained these directories as RETAINED_NON_CANONICAL because removing them would have meant deciding, inside a packaging increment, which layer owned the 44 governance symbols they held. P0-PKG-05 made those 44 ownership decisions (governance-ownership.lock.json) and relocated the code to PMFreak-owned space under src/lib/governance/authority, so both directories are now absent. The packages map below is retained as a deny-list: if either directory ever reappears, the gate still requires it to be non-canonical and correctly marked.
localCopies.constraint: Neither directory may exist. Should one be reintroduced, it may never declare, alias or otherwise resolve the names @aoc/protocol or @aoc-enterprise/runtime, and must carry the NON_CANONICAL_LEGACY_COPY marker.

privateFronteraWorkspaces.rationale: These are internal to the self-contained Frontera artifact and reach PMFreak only as its bundleDependencies. A direct PMFreak dependency or import would bypass the packaged boundary.

@aoc/protocol.sourceCommitNote: PR #387 was squash-merged; the RC source commit is not an ancestor of main but is retained on origin/claude/soberania-protocol-rc-package-fg02tq, and main (merge commit below) differs from it only in docs/release evidence files — no packaging input differs.
@aoc/protocol.reproductionProcedure: git worktree detached at sourceCommit; npm ci; npm run build; npm pack ./packages/protocol (node v22.22.2, npm 10.9.7)

@aoc-enterprise/runtime.sourceCommitNote: P0-PKG-07. Ancestor of Soberania-Enterprise main via the PR #112 merge commit below; verified locally with `git merge-base --is-ancestor`.
@aoc-enterprise/runtime.reproductionProcedure: git worktree detached at sourceCommit; npm ci; npm run build; npm pack . (node v22.22.2, npm 10.9.7). Reproduced bit-for-bit in this environment: the resulting tarball SHA-256 equalled the frozen value above before it was vendored, and npm pack itself reported "total files: 6362".
@aoc-enterprise/runtime.mergeCommitNote: Verified live: this SHA is the current head of Soberania-Enterprise main and its message names "Merge pull request #112 ... P0-PKG-07: productionize durable Frontera authority/recognition for external enforcement".
@aoc-enterprise/runtime.exportsFingerprintNote: Byte-identical to 1.0.0 and verified, not copied: the fingerprint covers the export MAP only, and P0-PKG-07 added its durable-authority surface to the existing ./enterprise and ./kernel subpaths without introducing a new one. Recomputed from the INSTALLED 1.1.0 manifest by scripts/check-packaged-aoc-artifacts.mjs on every run.

exportsFingerprintAlgorithm: sha256 of JSON.stringify(Object.keys(pkg.exports).sort().map((k) => [k, pkg.exports[k]])) — identical to scripts/fingerprint-public-surface.mjs (exportMap digest) in Soberania-Protocol/Soberania_Protocol
